description: Astro Br is a multidisciplinary team creating interactive web browser games to educate students about NASA and space. Our mission is to transform space science into accessible digital adventures through lightweight tech, pedagogical content, and inspiring visuals.
summary:
CtrlAstro is an interactive 2.5D web-based mission simulator designed to teach junior astronauts and STEM students the real engineering trade-offs of operating a lunar outpost at Shackleton Crater on the Moon's South Pole. Inspired by NASA's Artemis Program, players manage 15 mission days (or Endless Colony mode) by balancing limited Action Points and four critical life-support systems: Solar/Nuclear Power (VSAT & Kilopower), Cryogenic Oxygen (ISRU), Hydroponic Biomass, and Dipolar Radiation Shielding.

To make lunar science tangible and engaging, the simulator features an interactive R&D tech tree, tactical field dilemmas, and a scientifically validated Lunar Encyclopedia covering 10 real South Pole and space-weather phenomena—such as Cold-Trap Volatile Outgassing, Solar Particle Events, Moonquakes, and Electrostatic Dust Levitation—complete with real-time 2.5D visual animations and synthesized Web Audio cues. Built with React 19, TypeScript, Phaser 4, and Go, it runs free and ad-free on desktop and mobile browsers in English, Portuguese, and Spanish.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

CtrlAstro is a browser-based 2.5D isometric tactical simulator set inside Shackleton Crater at the Lunar South Pole. Acting as Base Commander, students allocate 3 to 5 daily Action Points (plus an emergency "+1 EVA" overdrive mechanic) to operate life-support modules, expand base infrastructure, research NASA technologies, and respond to tactical field anomalies across a 15-day mission toward orbital fleet docking.

EDUCATIONAL IMPACT FOR JUNIOR ASTRONAUTS

Rather than oversimplifying spaceflight, CtrlAstro turns real NASA engineering trade-offs into intuitive, fun decisions:

- Resource Interdependence: Running ISRU cryogenic oxygen extraction or biodome hydroponics drains power, while aligning Vertical Solar Arrays (VSAT) diverts life-support oxygen.

- Interactive Module Inspector: Clicking any 2.5D structure reveals its real NASA reference architecture (e.g., Artemis Surface Habitat, Kilopower KRUSTY, VIPER Rover), operational role, and engineering trade-offs.

- Scientifically Validated Lunar Encyclopedia ("Curiosities"): Students explore 10 real lunar hazards—including Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) cold-trap volatile outgassing, CME Solar Energetic Particle sparking, lobate scarps, and shallow tectonic moonquakes—and preview their 2.5D visual/audio simulations safely without damaging their base.

TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE & CREATIVE DESIGN

- Frontend & 2.5D Engine: Built with React 19, TypeScript, and Phaser 4 using a custom spherical-horizon isometric projection, HiDPI/Retina text rendering, multi-touch pinch-to-zoom, and adaptive layouts for desktop, tablet, and smartphone screens.

- Procedural Audio: Synthesized retro-futuristic telemetry chimes, alarms, and environmental soundscapes generated in real time via the Web Audio API (zero external audio asset bloat).

- Backend & Telemetry: RESTful API built in Go (Gin) supporting mission turn synchronization, live space-weather telemetry integration, and a persistent Global Commander Leaderboard, deployed on Vercel with full trilingual support (EN / PT / ES).
